tool.name: Estimator.single
tool.description: Estimate the total richness of a sample

param.label: calc - richness estimator
param.help: If not provided mothur uses erarefaction. The abundance based estimators (igabund, lnabund, lsabund, siabund) and the shift estimators (lnshift, sishift) fit a parametric distribution to the data instead of resampling it.
param.option: igrarefact - inverse Gaussian rarefaction with confidence intervals
lnrarefact - log normal rarefaction with confidence intervals
lsrarefact - log Student rarefaction with confidence intervals
sirarefact - Sichel rarefaction with confidence intervals
lnshift - log normal abundance with a shifted distribution
sishift - Sichel abundance with a shifted distribution

param.name: label
param.label: label - select OTU distance labels
param.help: all labels are used if none are selected

param.label: freq - frequency of the output
param.help: Output every freq sequence, or a percentage of the total number of sequences if below 1. Default 100

param.label: coverage - desired coverage when a single value is estimated
param.help: Only used by the rarefaction estimators. Default 0.80

tool.help:
@MOTHUR_OVERVIEW@
**Command Documentation**
The estimator.single_ command estimates the total richness of a sample from the observed abundances, using either a resampling (rarefaction) approach or a parametric distribution fitted to the abundance data. It takes a list_, rabund_, sabund_ or shared_ file.
The calc_ parameter selects the estimator; every estimator writes its own file, named after the calculator, so the estimates are returned as a collection with one element per calculator and label. The rarefaction estimators are evaluated at the sequence counts requested with freq_ (and at the coverage_ of the sample for the single value estimators), the distribution based ones fit the abundance distribution (invGauss, logNormal, logStudent or Sichel) by MCMC sampling, which makes them considerably slower.
